title: Chocolate Cake
intro: A tender two-layer cocoa sponge sandwiched and coated with a glossy dark chocolate ganache.
ingredients: 250 ml (1 cup) hot coffee or hot water
300 g (10 oz) dark chocolate, chopped, for the ganache
300 ml (1¼ cups) double cream, for the ganache
25 g (2 tbsp) butter, for the ganache
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Grease two 20 cm (8 in) round tins and line the bases with baking paper.
Sift the flour, cocoa, sugar, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and salt into a large bowl and whisk to combine.
In a jug, beat the eggs with the buttermilk, oil and vanilla. Pour into the dry ingredients and mix until smooth, then stir in the hot coffee; the batter will be thin.
Divide between the tins and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack to cool fully.
For the ganache, warm the cream until it just begins to steam, pour it over the chopped chocolate and leave for 2 minutes. Stir from the centre until glossy, then stir in the butter.
Let the ganache thicken at room temperature for about 30 minutes until spreadable.
Place one sponge on a plate, spread a third of the ganache over it and top with the second sponge. Cover the top and sides with the rest and leave to set before slicing.

title: Fudgy Brownies
intro: Dense, dark brownies with a crackly top and a soft, almost truffle-like middle.
ingredients: 185 g (¾ cup plus 1 tbsp) unsalted butter
100 g (3½ oz) milk or dark chocolate chips
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a 20 cm (8 in) square tin with baking paper.
Melt the butter and chopped dark chocolate together in a bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring now and then. Set aside to cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs, sugar and vanilla in a large bowl for 3 to 4 minutes until pale, thick and roughly doubled in volume.
Fold the cooled chocolate mixture into the eggs gently so you keep as much air as possible.
Sift the flour, cocoa and salt over the top and fold in until no streaks remain, then fold in the chocolate chips.
Pour into the tin, level the top and bake for 25 to 30 minutes. The edges should be set and the centre should still wobble slightly.
Cool completely in the tin before lifting out and cutting into 16 squares.

title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
intro: Chewy-centred cookies with crisp edges and generous pools of melted chocolate.
ingredients: 150 g (¾ cup) soft light brown sugar
250 g (9 oz) chocolate chips or chopped dark chocolate
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line two baking sheets with baking paper.
Beat the butter with both sugars until creamy and lighter in colour, about 2 minutes. Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Mix the flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt together, then stir into the butter mixture just until no dry flour shows.
Stir in the chocolate chips. Scoop heaped tablespoons of dough onto the trays, leaving 5 cm (2 in) between them.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the edges are golden but the centres still look a little soft. Sprinkle with flaky salt if using.
Leave on the trays for 5 minutes to firm up, then move to a rack to cool.

title: Hot Chocolate
intro: A thick, velvety mug of real melted chocolate and warm milk, finished with cream.
ingredients: 100 g (3½ oz) dark chocolate, finely chopped
steps: Pour the milk into a small saucepan and whisk in the cocoa, sugar and salt. Warm over medium heat, whisking, until steaming but not boiling.
Take the pan off the heat, add the chopped chocolate and let it sit for a minute to soften.
Whisk until the chocolate has melted completely and the drink is smooth and glossy, then stir in the vanilla.
Return to low heat for a minute if it needs reheating, then taste and adjust the sugar.
Pour into two mugs and top with a spoonful of whipped cream.

title: Chocolate Mousse
intro: A light, airy French mousse made from dark chocolate, whipped egg whites and softly whipped cream.
ingredients: 200 ml (¾ cup plus 1 tbsp) double cream
steps: Melt the chocolate and butter together in a bowl over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring occasionally. Remove from the heat and let it cool for 5 minutes.
Beat the egg yolks with the vanilla, then stir them into the warm chocolate until smooth.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and set aside in the fridge.
In a clean bowl, whisk the egg whites with the salt until foamy, then gradually add the sugar and whisk to soft, glossy peaks.
Fold a spoonful of the whites into the chocolate to loosen it, then fold in the rest of the whites in two additions, followed by the whipped cream, keeping the mixture light.
Spoon into six glasses or ramekins and chill for at least 4 hours. Serve topped with grated chocolate.

title: Tiramisu
intro: Coffee-soaked sponge fingers layered with a cloud of mascarpone cream and dusted with cocoa.
steps: Mix the cooled espresso with the liqueur, if using, in a shallow dish.

Whisk the egg yolks and sugar in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water for about 5 minutes, until pale, thick and warm. Remove from the heat and whisk for a minute more to cool slightly.
Beat the mascarpone briefly to loosen it, then fold it into the yolk mixture until smooth.
Whip the cream with the vanilla to soft peaks and fold it into the mascarpone mixture.
Dip the sponge fingers one at a time into the coffee for just a second or two per side and lay them in a single layer in a 20 x 30 cm (8 x 12 in) dish.
Spread half the mascarpone cream over the fingers, add a second layer of dipped fingers and finish with the remaining cream.
Cover and chill for at least 6 hours or overnight. Dust generously with cocoa and scatter with grated chocolate just before serving.

title: New York Cheesecake
intro: A tall, dense and creamy baked cheesecake on a buttery biscuit base, with a faint lemon tang.
ingredients: 200 g (7 oz) digestive biscuits or graham crackers, crushed
900 g (2 lb) full-fat cream cheese, at room temperature
200 ml (¾ cup plus 1 tbsp) soured cream
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Mix the biscuit crumbs with the melted butter, press firmly into the base of a 23 cm (9 in) springform tin and bake for 10 minutes. Cool while you make the filling.
Turn the oven up to 220 °C (425 °F). Wrap the outside of the tin in a double layer of foil.
Beat the cream cheese on low speed until smooth, then beat in the sugar, flour, vanilla, lemon zest and salt, scraping the bowl so there are no lumps.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating briefly after each, then mix in the soured cream. Avoid whipping air into the batter.
Pour the filling over the base. Bake for 10 minutes, then reduce the oven to 110 °C (225 °F) and bake for a further 60 to 70 minutes, until the edges are set and the centre still wobbles slightly.
Turn off the oven, open the door a crack and let the cheesecake sit inside for 1 hour to cool slowly and avoid cracks.
Run a knife around the edge, then cool fully and chill overnight before removing from the tin and slicing.

title: Carrot Cake
intro: A moist, spiced layer cake packed with grated carrot and walnuts, topped with tangy cream cheese frosting.
ingredients: 300 g (1½ cups) soft light brown sugar
250 g (9 oz) full-fat cream cheese, for the frosting
100 g (7 tbsp) unsalted butter, softened, for the frosting
300 g (2½ cups) icing sugar, for the frosting
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Grease and line two 20 cm (8 in) round tins.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt together in a bowl.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs with the brown sugar, oil and vanilla until smooth, then stir in the dry ingredients until just combined.
Fold in the grated carrot and most of the walnuts, keeping a handful back for decoration.
Divide between the tins and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until springy and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack.
For the frosting, beat the butter until smooth, add the cream cheese and beat briefly, then beat in the icing sugar until thick and spreadable. Do not over-beat or it will loosen.
Once the cakes are completely cold, sandwich them with half the frosting, spread the rest over the top and scatter with the reserved walnuts.

title: Red Velvet Cake
intro: A striking crimson cake with a subtle cocoa flavour, a fine soft crumb and white cream cheese frosting.
ingredients: 350 g (12 oz) full-fat cream cheese, for the frosting
115 g (½ cup) unsalted butter, softened, for the frosting
400 g (3⅓ cups) icing sugar, for the frosting
1 tsp vanilla extract, for the frosting
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Grease and line two 20 cm (8 in) round tins.
Sift the flour, cocoa and salt together and set aside.
Beat the butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time, followed by the vanilla and the red colouring.
Add the flour mixture in three additions, alternating with the buttermilk, mixing on low speed until just smooth.
Stir the bicarbonate of soda into the vinegar; it will fizz. Quickly fold it through the batter.
Divide between the tins and bake for 28 to 32 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool for 10 minutes in the tins, then turn out onto a rack and cool completely.
For the frosting, beat the butter and cream cheese together until smooth, then beat in the icing sugar and vanilla until thick.
Level the cakes if needed, fill with a third of the frosting and cover the top and sides with the rest. Crumble the trimmings over the top to decorate.

title: Victoria Sponge
intro: The classic British afternoon-tea cake: two light butter sponges filled with raspberry jam and whipped cream.
ingredients: 225 g (1 cup plus 2 tbsp) caster sugar
150 g (½ cup) raspberry or strawberry jam
200 ml (¾ cup plus 1 tbsp) double cream
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Grease two 20 cm (8 in) sandwich tins and line the bases.
Beat the butter and sugar together for 3 to 4 minutes until very pale and fluffy.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each and adding a spoonful of flour if the mixture starts to curdle. Beat in the vanilla.
Sift in the remaining flour and baking powder and fold in gently, then stir in the milk to give a batter that drops easily from the spoon.
Divide evenly between the tins, level the tops and bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until golden and springy to the touch.
Cool in the tins for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a rack and cool completely.
Whip the cream to soft peaks. Spread the jam over one sponge, top with the cream, sandwich with the other sponge and dust the top with icing sugar.

title: Lemon Drizzle Cake
intro: A buttery lemon loaf cake soaked while warm with a sharp, crunchy sugar syrup.
ingredients: 225 g (1 cup plus 2 tbsp) caster sugar
Juice of 2 lemons, for the drizzle
100 g (½ cup) granulated sugar, for the drizzle
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and line a 900 g (2 lb) loaf tin with baking paper.
Beat the butter and caster sugar until pale and fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and lemon zest, then add the milk to loosen the batter slightly.
Spoon into the tin, smooth the top and bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
While the cake bakes, stir the lemon juice and granulated sugar together without dissolving the sugar fully.
As soon as the cake comes out of the oven, prick it all over with a skewer and spoon the drizzle slowly over the top so it soaks in and the sugar forms a crust.
Leave in the tin until completely cold before lifting out and slicing.

title: Strawberry Shortcake
intro: Split sweet biscuits piled with sugared strawberries and softly whipped cream.
ingredients: 500 g (1 lb) strawberries, hulled and sliced
3 tbsp caster sugar, for the berries
50 g (¼ cup) caster sugar, for the biscuits
115 g (½ cup) cold unsalted butter, cubed
180 ml (¾ cup) cold double cream, plus 1 tbsp for brushing
300 ml (1¼ cups) double cream, for whipping
steps: Toss the sliced strawberries with the 3 tbsp sugar and leave for 30 minutes so they release their juices.
Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F) and line a baking sheet. Whisk the flour, 50 g sugar, baking powder and salt together, then rub in the cold butter until it looks like coarse crumbs.
Stir the 180 ml cream and vanilla in with a knife until the dough just comes together; it should be shaggy, not smooth.
Pat the dough out on a floured surface to about 2.5 cm (1 in) thick and cut six rounds with a 7 cm (3 in) cutter, re-patting the scraps once.
Brush the tops with cream and bake for 12 to 15 minutes until risen and golden. Cool on a rack for 10 minutes.
Whip the 300 ml cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks.
Split the warm biscuits, spoon strawberries and juice onto the bases, add a generous spoon of cream and replace the tops.

title: Apple Pie
intro: A double-crust pie with a flaky all-butter pastry and a tender, spiced apple filling.
ingredients: 1 tbsp caster sugar, for the pastry
250 g (1 cup plus 2 tbsp) cold unsalted butter, cubed
1.2 kg (2½ lb) mixed apples, such as Granny Smith and Braeburn, peeled and sliced
150 g (¾ cup) caster sugar, for the filling
2 tbsp plain flour, for the filling
25 g (2 tbsp) butter, cubed, for the filling
steps: Mix the flour, salt and 1 tbsp sugar, then rub in the cold butter until it resembles coarse crumbs with some pea-sized pieces. Add the ice water a spoonful at a time until the dough just holds together.
Divide into two discs, one slightly larger, wrap and chill for at least 1 hour.
Toss the apple slices with the 150 g sugar, 2 tbsp flour, cinnamon, nutmeg and lemon juice.
Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) with a baking sheet inside. Roll the larger disc out and line a 23 cm (9 in) pie dish, leaving an overhang.
Pile in the apples, dot with the cubed butter and roll the second disc over the top. Trim, fold the edges under and crimp, then cut a few slits in the lid.

Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with demerara sugar. Bake on the hot sheet for 20 minutes, then lower the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and bake for a further 40 to 45 minutes, until deep golden and the filling bubbles through the slits.
Cool for at least 1 hour so the juices thicken before slicing.

title: Pumpkin Pie
intro: A smooth, warmly spiced pumpkin custard baked in a crisp single pastry shell.
ingredients: 125 g (½ cup plus 1 tbsp) cold unsalted butter, cubed
150 g (¾ cup) soft light brown sugar
½ tsp salt, for the filling
300 ml (1¼ cups) double cream or evaporated milk
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and salt until crumbly, add just enough ice water to bring it together, then shape into a disc, wrap and chill for 1 hour.
Roll the pastry out and line a 23 cm (9 in) pie dish. Crimp the edge, prick the base and chill for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Line the pastry with baking paper, fill with baking beans and bake for 15 minutes, then remove the paper and beans and bake for 5 minutes more.
Whisk the pumpkin purée with the eggs, brown sugar, spices and salt until smooth, then whisk in the cream and vanilla.

Pour the filling into the warm pastry shell and bake at 200 °C (400 °F) for 15 minutes, then lower to 180 °C (350 °F) and bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until the edges are set and the centre has only a slight wobble.
Cool completely on a rack, then chill for at least 1 hour before serving with whipped cream.

title: Crème Brûlée
intro: A silky vanilla custard hidden beneath a thin sheet of crackling caramelised sugar.
ingredients: 1 vanilla pod, split, or 2 tsp vanilla extract
6 tbsp caster sugar, for the tops
steps: Heat the oven to 150 °C (300 °F). Put six ramekins in a deep roasting tin.
Warm the cream with the vanilla pod and its scraped seeds (or the extract) until steaming, then take off the heat and let it infuse for 10 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolks with the 75 g sugar and salt just until combined, then slowly pour in the warm cream, whisking gently to avoid foam.
Strain the custard into a jug and divide between the ramekins. Pour hot water into the tin to come halfway up the ramekins.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until the custards are set at the edges but still tremble in the centre. Lift out of the water and cool, then chill for at least 4 hours.

Just before serving, sprinkle an even layer of sugar over each custard and caramelise with a blowtorch (or under a very hot grill) until deep amber. Let the sugar harden for a minute before cracking in.

title: Panna Cotta
intro: A gently set, wobbling cream dessert from Piedmont, served here with a quick berry sauce.
ingredients: 3 sheets leaf gelatine (or 2 tsp powdered gelatine)
1 vanilla pod, split, or 2 tsp vanilla extract
250 g (9 oz) mixed berries, for the sauce
2 tbsp caster sugar, for the sauce
steps: Soak the gelatine sheets in cold water for 5 minutes until soft (or sprinkle powdered gelatine over 3 tbsp cold water and leave to swell).
Heat the cream, milk, sugar and vanilla in a pan until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is steaming; do not let it boil.
Take the pan off the heat, squeeze the water from the gelatine and stir it into the hot cream until completely dissolved. Remove the vanilla pod.
Strain into a jug and pour into six 150 ml (5 oz) moulds or glasses. Cool, then chill for at least 4 hours until set.
For the sauce, warm the berries with the sugar and lemon juice for 3 to 4 minutes until they start to collapse, then cool.
To unmould, dip each mould briefly in hot water and invert onto a plate. Spoon the berry sauce alongside.

title: Churros with Chocolate Sauce
intro: Crisp ridged fried dough sticks rolled in cinnamon sugar, with a thick dark chocolate dipping sauce.
ingredients: 1 tbsp caster sugar, for the dough
150 g (1 cup plus 3 tbsp) plain flour
1 litre (4 cups) vegetable oil, for frying
100 g (½ cup) caster sugar, for coating
150 g (5 oz) dark chocolate, chopped, for the sauce
200 ml (¾ cup plus 1 tbsp) whole milk, for the sauce
steps: Bring the water, butter, 1 tbsp sugar and salt to the boil in a pan. Tip in the flour all at once and beat with a wooden spoon over low heat for a minute until it forms a smooth ball that leaves the sides.
Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the egg until the dough is glossy. Spoon into a piping bag fitted with a large star nozzle.
For the sauce, whisk the cornflour and cocoa into a little of the milk, then heat with the rest of the milk until steaming. Add the chocolate and stir until thick and smooth. Keep warm.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 180 °C (350 °F). Mix the 100 g sugar with the cinnamon on a plate.
Pipe 12 cm (5 in) lengths of dough straight into the oil, cutting them off with scissors, and fry 4 or 5 at a time for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp.
Drain on kitchen paper, roll in the cinnamon sugar while hot and serve at once with the chocolate sauce.

title: Baklava
intro: Layers of crisp filo and ground pistachios or walnuts, baked golden and soaked in a lemony syrup.
ingredients: 400 g (14 oz) filo pastry, thawed if frozen
250 g (1 cup plus 2 tbsp) unsalted butter, melted
300 g (2½ cups) pistachios or walnuts, finely chopped
2 tbsp caster sugar, for the filling
300 g (1½ cups) granulated sugar, for the syrup
steps: Make the syrup first: simmer the 300 g sugar, water, honey, lemon juice and lemon peel for 10 minutes until slightly thickened, then leave to cool completely.
Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Mix the chopped nuts with the cinnamon and 2 tbsp sugar. Brush a 23 x 33 cm (9 x 13 in) tin with butter.
Lay half the filo sheets in the tin one at a time, brushing each with melted butter and keeping the rest covered with a damp cloth so they do not dry out.
Spread the nut mixture evenly over the pastry, then layer on the remaining sheets, buttering each one, and brush the top generously.
With a sharp knife, cut all the way through into diamonds or squares before baking.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Pour the cold syrup slowly over the hot baklava so it sizzles and soaks in. Leave at room temperature for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight, before serving.

title: Mochi Daifuku
intro: Soft, chewy rice-flour mochi wrapped around sweet red bean paste, the classic Japanese tea-time sweet.
ingredients: 150 g (1 cup) glutinous rice flour (shiratamako or mochiko)
240 g (8½ oz) sweet red bean paste (anko)
50 g (⅓ cup) cornflour or potato starch, for dusting
A drop of pink food colouring (optional)
steps: Divide the red bean paste into eight portions, roll each into a ball and chill while you make the mochi.
Whisk the rice flour, sugar and water in a heatproof bowl until smooth, adding the colouring if using.

Cover the bowl and microwave on high for 1 minute, stir, then microwave for a further 1 to 2 minutes in 30-second bursts, stirring in between, until the dough is thick, glossy and translucent. Alternatively steam the covered bowl for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring halfway.
Dust a work surface generously with cornflour and turn the hot dough out onto it. Dust the top, then press and cut it into eight equal pieces.
Working while the dough is warm, flatten a piece into a 9 cm (3½ in) disc with floured hands, set a ball of bean paste in the centre and pinch the edges up and together to seal.
Turn seam-side down, dust off the excess starch and repeat with the rest. Serve the same day at room temperature.

title: Pavlova
intro: A crisp-shelled meringue with a marshmallow centre, heaped with whipped cream and fresh fruit.
ingredients: 6 large egg whites, at room temperature
300 g (10 oz) strawberries, hulled and halved
steps: Heat the oven to 150 °C (300 °F). Draw a 23 cm (9 in) circle on baking paper, flip it over onto a baking sheet.

Whisk the egg whites with the salt until they hold soft peaks, then add the sugar a tablespoon at a time, whisking until the meringue is stiff and glossy and no longer feels grainy when rubbed between your fingers.
Fold in the cornflour, vinegar and vanilla.
Spoon the meringue onto the circle, building the sides up slightly higher than the centre so there is a shallow well for the topping.

Put in the oven, immediately reduce the temperature to 120 °C (250 °F) and bake for 1 hour 15 minutes until the shell is dry and pale. Turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside with the door ajar until completely cold.
Shortly before serving, whip the cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks, pile it into the centre and top with the strawberries, kiwi and passion fruit pulp.

title: Banana Bread
intro: A moist, tender loaf that turns overripe bananas into something worth getting up for.
ingredients: 3 very ripe bananas (about 350 g / 12 oz peeled)
150 g (¾ cup) soft light brown sugar
75 g (¾ cup) walnuts or pecans, chopped (optional)
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F) and line a 900 g (2 lb) loaf tin with baking paper.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl until mostly smooth with a few small lumps.
Stir in the melted butter, brown sugar, egg and vanilla until well combined.
Mix the flour, bicarbonate of soda, cinnamon and salt together, then fold into the banana mixture just until no dry patches remain. Fold in the nuts if using.
Pour into the tin and bake for 55 to 60 minutes, until the top is deep golden and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. Cover loosely with foil if it browns too fast.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then lift out onto a rack to cool before slicing.

title: Cinnamon Rolls
intro: Soft enriched dough swirled with cinnamon butter, baked until golden and glazed while warm.
ingredients: 75 g (5 tbsp) unsalted butter, melted, for the dough
500 g (4 cups) strong white bread flour
100 g (7 tbsp) unsalted butter, softened, for the filling
100 g (½ cup) soft light brown sugar
Pearl sugar or a simple icing-sugar glaze, to finish
steps: Stir the yeast and a pinch of the sugar into the lukewarm milk and leave for 5 to 10 minutes until frothy.
Add the remaining sugar, egg, melted butter, cardamom and salt, then work in the flour to make a soft dough. Knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Put the dough in an oiled bowl, cover and leave in a warm place for about 1 hour until doubled in size.
Beat the softened butter with the brown sugar and cinnamon to make a spreadable paste.
Roll the dough out on a floured surface into a rectangle about 30 x 40 cm (12 x 16 in). Spread the filling right to the edges, roll up tightly from a long side and cut into 12 slices.
Arrange the slices cut-side up in a lined 23 x 33 cm (9 x 13 in) tin or in paper cases, cover and leave to rise for 45 minutes to 1 hour until puffy.
Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Brush the rolls with beaten egg, scatter with pearl sugar if using, and bake for 18 to 22 minutes until golden.
Cool for 10 minutes; if glazing instead of using pearl sugar, drizzle with icing-sugar glaze while still warm.

title: Chocolate Lava Cake
intro: Individual dark chocolate cakes with a set outer crumb and a molten centre that flows when cut.
ingredients: 115 g (½ cup) unsalted butter, plus extra for the ramekins
1 tbsp cocoa powder, for dusting the ramekins
steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Butter four 175 ml (6 oz) ramekins thoroughly, dust the insides with cocoa and tap out the excess.
Melt the butter and chocolate together gently over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring until smooth. Cool for a few minutes.
Whisk the eggs, egg yolks, sugar and salt vigorously for 2 to 3 minutes until pale and thickened, then whisk in the vanilla.
Fold the melted chocolate into the egg mixture, then sift over the flour and fold in just until combined.
Divide between the ramekins and set on a baking sheet. Bake for 11 to 13 minutes, until the edges are firm and the tops are set but the centres still look soft.
Rest for 1 minute, run a knife around the edges and turn each cake out onto a plate. Serve immediately.

title: Flan / Crème Caramel
intro: A smooth baked milk custard turned out so its amber caramel runs down the sides.
ingredients: 200 g (1 cup) granulated sugar, for the caramel
1 x 397 g (14 oz) can sweetened condensed milk
1 x 410 g (12 fl oz) can evaporated milk
steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C (325 °F). Put the sugar and water in a small pan over medium heat and cook without stirring, swirling the pan occasionally, until it turns a deep amber, 8 to 10 minutes.
Immediately pour the caramel into a 23 cm (9 in) round cake tin or flan dish and tilt to coat the base. Leave to harden.
Whisk the eggs, egg yolks, vanilla and salt together gently, then whisk in the condensed milk, evaporated milk and whole milk until smooth without creating much foam.
Strain the custard over the set caramel. Set the tin in a roasting tray and pour in hot water to come halfway up the sides.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes, until the custard is set at the edges and just wobbles in the centre when nudged.
Lift from the water bath, cool to room temperature, then cover and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Run a thin knife around the edge, place a rimmed serving plate on top and invert in one confident motion so the caramel pools around the flan.

title: Gulab Jamun
intro: Soft milk-solid dumplings fried to a deep brown and steeped in a cardamom and rose-scented syrup.
ingredients: 400 g (2 cups) granulated sugar, for the syrup
2 tbsp ghee or melted butter, plus 500 ml (2 cups) ghee or vegetable oil for frying
steps: Simmer the sugar, water, cardamom and saffron for 8 to 10 minutes until slightly syrupy but not thick. Stir in the rose water and keep warm.

Mix the milk powder, flour and baking powder in a bowl, rub in the 2 tbsp ghee, then add the milk a spoonful at a time and bring together into a soft, smooth dough without kneading hard. Rest for 10 minutes.
Grease your palms and roll the dough into 20 small, completely smooth balls with no cracks.
Heat the frying ghee or oil in a deep pan over low-medium heat to about 150 °C (300 °F); a test piece should rise slowly and brown gently.
Fry the balls in batches, keeping them moving so they colour evenly, for 6 to 8 minutes until deep golden brown all over.
Drain briefly and drop the hot jamuns straight into the warm syrup. Leave to soak for at least 1 hour, during which they will swell and soften.
Serve warm or at room temperature with a little syrup and a sprinkle of pistachios.
